cycles.en_text_before_rewrite:
# The Fee Plan Changed, but Crude Prices Returned to Highs. Fears Over the Strait Remain

“Cargo passing through will pay a 20 percent reimbursement fee.” The fee plan that surfaced over the Strait of Hormuz took a different form the next day.

But oil prices did not respond with, “If the plan has changed, we can relax now.”

Trump’s first post proposed asking all cargo passing through the strait to pay a fee to cover the cost of keeping it safe. The fee would apply to more than just crude oil.

The next day, Trump named trade with the United States and investment projects by Gulf states instead of the fee. He said the decision followed “very productive talks” with Middle Eastern leaders. The proposal changed overnight, from a fee to trade and investment.

So did the oil market settle down right away? No.

After the announcement, Brent futures briefly gave up some of their gains. It seemed the market had relaxed a little, but the move did not last. Before long, prices returned to a high level close to where they had been before the announcement. At the time the article was published, they were up about 2.6 percent and above $85 a barrel.

Reports said that, at that point, concerns continued over attacks between the United States and Iran, a sea blockade, and the safety of tankers. What can be confirmed is that concerns about safety remained. It would not be accurate to say that tanker safety had not been ensured.

The fee plan was dropped. But worries about the route used to transport energy did not disappear. Oil prices’ gains narrowed only briefly. Even after the proposal changed, concerns about supply remained, and prices did not settle down right away.

## In one line
Oil prices soon returned near their pre-announcement highs, despite Trump dropping the proposed Hormuz shipping fee.

verdicts.claim: # The Fee Plan Changed, but Crude Prices Returned to Highs. Fears Over the Strait Remain
verdicts.reason: HF-007とHF-009に、トランプ氏が料案を置き換えたこと、Brentが発表前に近い高水準へ戻り、海峡の懸念が続いたことが一致する。

verdicts.claim: “Cargo passing through will pay a 20 percent reimbursement fee.”
verdicts.reason: 20％と全貨物の範囲はHF-002に沿うが、Ledgerは提案として記録し、支払義務者も特定していないため、「貨物が支払う」と断定する点が相手先・限定条件で一致しない。

verdicts.claim: But oil prices did not respond with, “If the plan has changed, we can relax now.”
verdicts.reason: 価格がすぐ落ち着いたわけではないという修辞的表現は、HF-009の一時的な上げ幅縮小後に高水準へ戻った動きと一致する。

verdicts.claim: So did the oil market settle down right away?
verdicts.reason: 市場がすぐ落ち着いたかを尋ねる修辞的な問いで、独立した事実を追加していない。

verdicts.claim: It seemed the market had relaxed a little, but the move did not last.
verdicts.reason: 「少し落ち着いた」後に動きが続かなかったという記述は、HF-009の一時的な上げ幅縮小と、その後の高水準への回復に一致する。

verdicts.claim: It would not be accurate to say that tanker safety had not been ensured.
verdicts.reason: タンカーの安全が確保されていないとは言えない、という否定表現は安全確保を示唆するが、Ledgerが裏付けるのは安全上の懸念の継続であり、安全確保の状態は確認していない。

verdicts.claim: Oil prices soon returned near their pre-announcement highs, despite Trump dropping the proposed Hormuz shipping fee.
verdicts.reason: HF-007の料案の置換と、HF-009の発表後に価格が一時的に上げ幅を縮めてから発表前に近い高水準へ戻ったとの記録に一致する。

verdicts.claim: So did the oil market settle down right away?
verdicts.reason: C4と同じ、市場がすぐ落ち着いたかを尋ねる修辞的な問いで、独立した事実を追加していない。
